hypotheses.title: Every symbol lookup takes the global symbolSpacesMu RWMutex read lock; concurrent stage 5-9 goroutines contend on its reader counter
hypotheses.issue: CompilerEnvironment.GetSymbol (and SymbolPackage, AddSymbolToSameSpace, CreateNarrowedSymbol) call symbolSpace(index), which takes the global symbolSpacesMu.RLock()+deferred RUnlock just to index the append-only symbolSpaces slice. Every variable reference / SymbolType / ValueSymbolMetadata query in type resolution, semantic analysis, CFG and desugaring goes through it. Stage 5 resolves function bodies in parallel goroutines (type_resolver.go:ResolvePrivateNodes) and stages 5-9 run concurrently across modules, so all cores do atomic adds on the same RWMutex reader count (single shared cache line). On the reproducer the atomic add inside RLock/RUnlock was ~57% of stage-5 CPU; the global RLock cost >10x more per call than the per-space SymbolSpace.SymbolAt RLock that is called equally often, i.e. it is cache-line contention rather than intrinsic lock cost. Spaces are only ever appended (NewSymbolSpace, from NewFunctionScope/NewBlockScope), never removed or replaced, so reads don't need the lock. The effect scales with core count and number of concurrently compiled modules/functions.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a multi-module Ballerina package whose function bodies are dominated by
plain local-variable references (each resolves symbols through CompilerEnvironment.GetSymbol)."""
import os, sys
out = sys.argv[1]; M = int(sys.argv[2]); F = int(sys.argv[3]); S = int(sys.argv[4])
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
open(os.path.join(out, "Ballerina.toml"), "w").write('[package]\norg = "perf"\nname = "symlookup"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n')
def body(m, f):
    L = [f"public function f{f}(int a, int b, int c) returns int {{"]
    L.append("    int x0 = a + b + c;")
    for s in range(1, S):
        L.append(f"    int x{s} = x{s-1} + a * b - c + x{s-1} * a + b;")
    L.append(f"    return x{S-1};")
    L.append("}")
    return "\n".join(L)
for m in range(M):
    d = os.path.join(out, "modules", f"m{m}"); os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(d, f"m{m}.bal"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write("\n\n".join(body(m, f) for f in range(F)) + "\n")
imports = "\n".join(f"import symlookup.m{m};" for m in range(M))
calls = "\n".join(f"    t += m{m}:f0(1, 2, 3) % 7;" for m in range(M))
open(os.path.join(out, "main.bal"), "w").write(f"import ballerina/io;\n{imports}\n\npublic function main() {{\n    int t = 0;\n{calls}\n    io:println(t);\n}}\n")

hypotheses.fix_approach: Store the symbol-space list as atomic.Pointer[[]*model.SymbolSpace]. NewSymbolSpace keeps a (plain) mutex to serialize appends: load the current slice, create the space with index len(spaces), append, Store(&spaces). Appending in place into the shared backing array is safe because every previously published slice header only reads up to its own length and the atomic store/load provides happens-before. symbolSpace() becomes (*c.symbolSpaces.Load())[index-1] with no lock; FindSymbol iterates the loaded snapshot without copying. NewCompilerEnvironment stores an empty slice so Load() is never nil. The RWMutex becomes a sync.Mutex since nothing reads under it. Also tried making SymbolSpace.SymbolAt (model/symbol.go per-space RLock) lock-free: no measurable extra gain and one extra allocation per symbol append, so it was dropped. make test and make test-race both pass.

notes: Side observation (unverified, not a perf issue): the exploration agent reported a deeply indented file (e.g. 200 nested `if`s indented 4 spaces per level) panics with `diagnostics: StartLine: failed to resolve startOffset -47314`. Also noted CFG stage walks each function AST three times (buildImplicitInitState, deferredFinalLocals, collectLambdaFunctions), ~4% on large benches.
